meta.note: Synthetic fixture. No real business, customer, phone number, or evidence is represented.

categories.name: Understand
categories.question: Can a visitor understand what is offered, where, for whom, and what to do next?

categories.name: Contact
categories.question: Can a ready visitor become a lead without friction or a dead end?

categories.name: Respond and Book
categories.question: Does the visible experience support a fast, qualified continuation?

categories.name: Trust
categories.question: Does the business provide enough credible proof to act?

categories.name: Mobile and Technical
categories.question: Can the customer actually use the experience on a phone?

categories.name: Findability
categories.question: Can a qualified local prospect discover useful pages?

checks.title: Service clarity
evidence: M-01: hero says "Plumbing done right" but not the service or city above the fold.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Name the service in the hero in plain language.

checks.title: Location and service-area clarity
evidence: M-01 and contact page: Example City and a 25-mile service area are visible.
checks.recommendedIntervention: State the city/service area and add local proof.

checks.title: Customer problem and outcome clarity
evidence: M-01 and service page: "fast repairs" is present; the homeowner outcome is vague.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Name the customer problem and the outcome.

checks.title: Primary action clarity
evidence: M-01, D-01: one "Get an estimate" button dominates the hero.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use one dominant next step above the fold.

checks.title: Offer specificity and price anchor
evidence: M-01, service pages: no price, starting-at price, or range.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add a starting-at price or range for a core job.

checks.title: Service navigation
evidence: Mobile menu: Services opens a list; drain and water-heater pages are two taps away.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Put the top services in the main navigation.

checks.title: Service-area eligibility navigation
evidence: Service-area page lists Example City and four neighboring cities.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add a service-area list, map, or ZIP check.

checks.title: Language access
checks.na_reason: multilingual access not configured for this market
evidence: N/A: the synthetic audit is configured for English only.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add the configured language path and translate conversion pages.

checks.title: Phone visible and consistent
evidence: M-01, contact page, footer: (555) 010-0200 appears consistently.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use one visible phone number consistently.

checks.title: Click-to-call on mobile
evidence: M-01 DOM: tel:+15550100200 in the sticky action bar.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Make the mobile phone a tel: link in a persistent action.

checks.title: Text/SMS path
checks.na_reason: optional module disabled for this market
evidence: N/A: SMS module disabled for this audit.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add a working sms: link when SMS is enabled.

checks.title: Form exists and is reachable
evidence: Contact page is one tap from the header and renders a six-field form.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Make the lead form reachable in two taps.

checks.title: Form friction
evidence: Contact form: name, phone, email, ZIP, service, message; message is not required.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Cut fields to name, phone, ZIP, and problem.

checks.title: Form usability
evidence: Mobile form: labels and input types are present; the ZIP field uses autocomplete="postal-code"; submit is visible.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add labels, input types, autocomplete, and a reachable submit.

checks.title: Online scheduler or booking
evidence: Book path: scheduler iframe loads and shows availability; no appointment selected.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add a working scheduler with live availability.

checks.title: No conversion dead end
evidence: M-01, service page, about page: each ends with a next step; reviews page relies on the persistent header action.
checks.recommendedIntervention: End every high-intent page with a next step.

checks.title: Chat or callback request
checks.na_reason: optional module disabled for this market
evidence: N/A: chat/callback module disabled for this audit.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add a human-backed chat or callback when enabled.

checks.title: Response and acknowledgement promise
evidence: Form area: "We will be in touch soon." No time, channel, or hours.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Publish a response time, channel, and hours.

checks.title: After-hours or emergency path
evidence: Header: "Mon-Sat 7am-7pm" plus an emergency call link.
checks.recommendedIntervention: State hours and the after-hours or emergency path.

checks.title: Booking path steps and mobile usability
evidence: Mobile path: book is two taps from the home page; scheduler is usable but opens a third-party page.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Reduce booking steps and keep the path on-site.

checks.title: Confirmation expectations
evidence: Form area: generic "we will contact you" only.
checks.recommendedIntervention: State what happens after submission and when.

checks.title: Qualification context without over-asking
evidence: Form asks service, ZIP, problem, and phone; no account required.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Capture service, ZIP or area, problem, and contact preference.

checks.title: Estimate or quote request workflow
evidence: Service pages link to "Request an estimate" with a scope field and photo upload.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add an estimate request with scope and a clear next step.

checks.title: Review volume, source, and profile link
evidence: Reviews widget shows 4.7 stars and 38 reviews with a link to the external profile.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Show rating, count, source, and a profile link.

checks.title: Specific testimonials and case studies
evidence: Two named testimonials with job type; no photos or specific numbers.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add named stories with job type and outcome.

checks.title: Real project proof
evidence: Gallery has four uncaptioned job photos.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Caption real job photos with city, job, and result.

checks.title: License, insurance, and certifications
evidence: Footer: license number, insured statement, and manufacturer badge.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Show license, insurance, and relevant certifications.

checks.title: Guarantee and warranty specificity
evidence: Service page: "warranty" with no term or scope.
checks.recommendedIntervention: State the warranty term and scope.

checks.title: Identity and differentiation consistency
evidence: About page names the owner and a "same-day repair" claim; the footer uses a different company name.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use one identity and one verifiable differentiator.

checks.title: Mobile LCP
evidence: Lighthouse mobile median LCP 3.1 s across 3 runs.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Compress the hero and defer non-critical scripts.

checks.title: Mobile layout usability
evidence: M-01: one hero heading clips at 390px; menu opens; form fields visible.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Fix viewport, text size, clipping, and menu usability.

checks.title: Tap targets and persistent action
evidence: M-01: sticky call button; three footer links are under 44px.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use 44px targets and a persistent action.

checks.title: HTTPS and security
evidence: URL loads over HTTPS with a valid certificate.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Serve HTTPS with a valid certificate.

checks.title: Broken links, CTAs, and conversion-blocking errors
evidence: One service page link 404s; the primary estimate path still works.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Fix broken links, CTAs, forms, and conversion-blocking errors.

checks.title: Title, meta description, and H1
evidence: Title and meta include plumbing and Example City; H1 is brand-only.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Put service and city in title, meta, and H1.

checks.title: Indexability
evidence: Canonical present, robots allow indexing, sitemap.xml returns 200.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Fix canonical, robots, and sitemap.

checks.title: Local schema and NAP consistency
evidence: LocalBusiness schema present; visible NAP matches the footer.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add LocalBusiness or Service schema and consistent NAP.

checks.title: Service and location pages with unique content
evidence: No dedicated city pages; one service-area list only.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Build unique service and location pages.

checks.title: Analytics present
evidence: GA4 and Google Tag Manager are present.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Install GA4, GTM, or an equivalent analytics platform.

evidence: No conversion events or ads tags detected.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add conversion events and ads or call tracking.

topLeaks.title: Mobile estimate form is difficult to complete
No observable immediate acknowledgement after a form submit
Unclosed estimates may not receive follow-up

ownerDataRequired.title: Speed-to-lead
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: A fast first response is often the difference between a booked job and a competitor's job. The public site cannot prove response time.
questions: What is the median time from lead to first human response?
How does that change by lead source (call, form, chat, text, ads)?
Who owns new leads during business hours and after hours?
How many contact attempts are made before a lead is abandoned?
How many inbound calls are missed or abandoned each week?

ownerDataRequired.title: After-hours and emergency handling
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Emergency demand does not wait for office hours. A visible emergency path is not proof that a human answers it.
questions: What happens to a call or form submitted after hours?
Is there an on-call rotation or answering service?
What percentage of after-hours leads become jobs?
Are emergency jobs priced or prioritized differently?

ownerDataRequired.title: Lead quality and routing
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: A form can collect data and still fail to route the right job to the right person.
questions: Which form fields are actually used to qualify or route a lead?
What percentage of form leads are spam, out of area, or the wrong service?
Where do form leads land, and who sees them?
What information is missing most often when the office calls back?

ownerDataRequired.title: Booking capacity and confirmation
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: An online booking can create a bad customer experience if the calendar is wrong or the office cannot absorb the slot.
questions: How many booked jobs are rescheduled or cancelled each week?
Is the online calendar connected to real crew capacity?
Who confirms appointments, and when?
What happens when the requested slot is unavailable?

ownerDataRequired.title: Estimate pipeline
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Open estimates are often the largest recoverable revenue pool. The website cannot show how many exist.
questions: How many estimates are currently open?
What is the total value of open estimates?
What is the average time from request to estimate delivered?
What percentage of estimates are accepted?
What percentage of estimate requests never receive an estimate?

ownerDataRequired.title: Estimate close rate by source and size
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: The same website can produce very different revenue depending on close rate, job size, and lead source.
questions: What is the close rate by lead source?
What is the close rate by job size or service line?
What is the average job value?
Which objections appear most often on estimates?
Which lost reasons are recorded?

ownerDataRequired.title: Estimate follow-up
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Unclosed estimates are a high-value opportunity that a public website audit cannot observe.
questions: What percentage of open estimates receive follow-up?
How quickly is the first follow-up made?
How many attempts are made before follow-up stops?
Which channels are used (call, text, email)?
Are estimates segmented by size, service, or age?
Are stale estimates reactivated on a schedule?

ownerDataRequired.title: Customer history and job completion
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Repeat and referral revenue depends on knowing who bought, what was installed, and when the next service is due.
questions: How many past customers are in the CRM?
Is job history, equipment age, and service date recorded?
Is there a post-job check-in?
How many customers buy a second service within 12 months?

ownerDataRequired.title: Review requests
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: A strong review profile is public, but the review-request process is not.
questions: Are customers automatically asked for a review?
How soon after the job is the ask made?
Is the ask sent by SMS, email, or in person?
Is the process measured by technician or job type?
Is negative feedback captured before it becomes a public review?

ownerDataRequired.title: Referral operations
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Referrals are often the lowest-cost lead source, but they are rarely visible on the website.
questions: Do you ask for referrals? When and how?
Is there a referral offer or tracking method?
What percentage of new customers come from referrals?
Are referral partners (realtors, property managers, adjacent trades) tracked?
Is referral follow-up owned by someone?

ownerDataRequired.title: Reactivation and repeat business
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Old leads, unsold estimates, and inactive customers can produce revenue without new ad spend.
questions: How many past customers are inactive for 12+ months?
How many unsold estimates are older than 30, 60, or 90 days?
Are seasonal services or maintenance visits scheduled automatically?
Is there a maintenance plan or membership list?
Has anyone contacted the inactive list in the last year?

ownerDataRequired.title: Marketing attribution and channel profitability
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Tags can show that traffic arrived; only business data can show which channel produces closed revenue.
questions: Is lead source recorded on every lead and job?

How much is spent on ads, and what is the return?
